title: Local shifted dualizing lines and normalized section-chart comparisons
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $N\geq1$ with $NA=0$, and let $S$ be Noetherian with $N$ invertible on $S$. Work in the ordinary unbounded categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves, with exact inverse images. For every compactifiable structural map $b$ write $\omega_b=b^\times A$ using the right adjoint of $Rb_!$. Put $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$ and $A_T(d)=A_T(1)^{\otimes d}$, with $A_T(0)=A_T$.
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $d\geq0$, and let $g:V\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$, with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, $g s=1_S$.
For the ideal $\mathcal I$ of $s(S)$ set $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$, $\pi:N_s=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to S$, with zero section $z$. Set $D_sV=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$, using the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $t$ and the $b/t$, $b\in\mathcal I$. Its structural map is $q:D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and its section $\sigma$ is the augmentation $t\mapsto t$, $\mathcal I/t\mapsto0$, with coefficients restricted by $s$.
Assume $g,q,\pi$ are compactifiable and that $D_sV$ is Noetherian, $q$ is smooth separated of dimension $d$, with the canonical pairs $(g,s)$ at $1$ and $(\pi,z)$ at $0$. Write $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$, $C=s^*\omega_g$, $F=\sigma^*\omega_q$. Then $C[-2d]$ and $F[-2d]$ are locally constant sheaves, etale locally free of rank one. The counit-defined exceptional base-change maps give isomorphisms
$$\theta:i_1^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}C,\qquad\eta:i_0^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}z^*\omega_\pi.$$
On each affine centred etale coordinate neighbourhood $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ whose square of centres is Cartesian, the right-adjoint locality maps and the affine-space adjunction identify $C|_{S_i}$ with $A_{S_i}(d)[2d]$ and $F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$ with $A_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}(d)[2d]$. Thus there is an isomorphism $\lambda_i:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}\to a_i^*(C|_{S_i})$ obtained from these two identifications and Tate pullback. If $h_i=(i_1^*\lambda_i)\theta_i^{-1}$, then
$$\lambda_i^{\mathrm{norm}}=a_i^*(h_i^{-1})\lambda_i,\qquad i_1^*\lambda_i^{\mathrm{norm}}=\theta_i.$$
All comparisons here are in the ordinary etale categories; the locality maps compare adjunctions by their counits, and no arbitrary fibre identification is substituted.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality].

source.place: Opening paragraph and Local construction, affine-space adjunction and correction at one; old item Steps 7–9.

proof.text: First check the bases for smooth duality. Since $g$ is finite type and $S$ is Noetherian, $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The same lemma applies to $\mathbf A^1_S$, whose polynomial coordinate algebra has one generator. The hypothesis already makes $D_sV$ Noetherian. Invertibility of $N$ persists because a ring homomorphism sends units to units. Apply [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] to $g$ and $q$: their dualizing objects shifted by $[-2d]$ are locally constant sheaves locally isomorphic to the coefficient sheaf. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] commutes with shifts and carries a degree-zero sheaf to its inverse image. Pulling a trivializing etale cover back along $s$ or $\sigma$ still trivializes its inverse image. Hence $C[-2d]$ and $F[-2d]$ are locally constant rank-one sheaves, as asserted.

source.place: Opening paragraph, shifted locally constant dualizing lines

proof.text: For $r=0,1$, apply [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] to $q$ and $i_r:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$, with coefficient object $A$. Its hypotheses hold: $q$ is smooth, separated, compactifiable, of dimension $d$, and both bases are Noetherian; the fibre structural maps are the assumed compactifiable $g$ and $\pi$. It gives the actual counit-transpose isomorphisms $j_1^*\omega_q\to\omega_g$ and $j_0^*\omega_q\to\omega_\pi$, where $j_r$ denotes the fibre inclusion. Pull back along the fibre sections. The identities $j_1s=\sigma i_1$ and $j_0z=\sigma i_0$, with the module inverse-image compositors of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], give precisely $\theta:i_1^*F\to C$ and $\eta:i_0^*F\to z^*\omega_\pi$. Exact inverse images descend termwise to these unbounded categories by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. These are the specified maps because we have used the counit-defined comparisons themselves.

source.place: Opening paragraph, restrictions to the two fibres

proof.text: Choose affine centred coordinates $e_i:U_i\to\mathbf A^d_{S_i}$ from [lem-trf-smooth-section-centred-coordinates], with $S_i$ an affine open cover of $S$ and $U_i$ an affine open neighbourhood of the section in $V_i=V\times_SS_i$. Write $g_i:V_i\to S_i$, $u_i:U_i\hookrightarrow V_i$, and $p_i:\mathbf A^d_{S_i}\to S_i$. The square of centres is Cartesian, not merely a pointwise equality. All maps to which locality will be applied are between Noetherian schemes and are compactifiable: base changes of $g,q$ are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; the chart maps are separated etale finite type; their structural composites are separated finite type. Polynomial affine spaces and these finite-type sources are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Over each affine Noetherian base they are compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification]. The open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; they are separated, and finite type here since their sources are quasi-compact opens in Noetherian schemes. The same checks apply to the deformed charts below.

source.place: Local construction, centred affine charts and locality hypotheses

proof.text: For an affine-space projection $p:\mathbf A^d_T\to T$ with a Noetherian base as above, [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] supplies a right adjoint $K\mapsto p^*K(d)[2d]$ to $Rp_!$ on the entire unbounded category. Compare it with the chosen $p^\times$ by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Choose the unique isomorphism whose image under $Rp_!$, followed by the target counit, is the source counit. Evaluating at $A_T$, and using the canonical isomorphism $p^{-1}A_T\cong A_{\mathbf A^d_T}$ of constant coefficient rings [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], identifies $\omega_p$ with $A_{\mathbf A^d_T}(d)[2d]$. Pulling to the zero section identifies $0^*\omega_p$ with $A_T(d)[2d]$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Thus the identification compares adjunctions by their counits; it does not select an arbitrary isomorphism of rank-one fibres. This construction also applies to $T=\mathbf A^1_{S_i}$.

Base change $g$ to $S_i$ using [prop-asd-smooth-base-change]. After section pullback this identifies $C|_{S_i}$ with $s_i^*\omega_{g_i}$. Apply [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] to $u_i$ over $S_i$ and to $e_i$ over $S_i$. Since $g_i u_i=p_i e_i$, their locality isomorphisms give $u_i^*\omega_{g_i}\cong\omega_{g_i u_i}\cong e_i^*\omega_{p_i}$. The comparisons are normalized by the unique counit-compatible right-adjoint comparison [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Pull back along the section in $U_i$. The equalities $u_i s_{U_i}=s_i$ and $e_i s_{U_i}=0_i$, using [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], identify the result with $0_i^*\omega_{p_i}$. Step 4 therefore gives an isomorphism $c_i:C|_{S_i}\to A_{S_i}(d)[2d]$.

source.place: Local construction, chart identification of the section dualizing object

proof.text: The standard pair has deformation algebra $R_i[x][t,(x)/t]=R_i[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$, with $x_j=tu_j$. Indeed the latter polynomial algebra maps into $R_i[x,t,t^{-1}]$ by $u_j\mapsto x_j/t$; distinct monomials $t^a u^b$ map to distinct Laurent monomials $t^{a-|b|}x^b$, so this is injective over any $R_i$, and its image is exactly the stated generated subalgebra. Apply [lem-trf-section-rees-base-change-etale] first to $S_i\to S$, then to the etale maps of pairs $u_i$ and $e_i$. This gives a deformed open neighbourhood of $\sigma(\mathbf A^1_{S_i})$ with a separated etale finite-type map to $\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$, preserving its zero section. Use [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] for restriction of $q$ to this base, followed by [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] for the two deformed chart maps. As in Step 5, their equal structural composites and the counit-compatible comparison of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identify the restriction of $F$ with the zero-section pullback of the standard affine-space dualizing object. Step 4 over $\mathbf A^1_{S_i}$ gives $f_i:F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}\to A_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}(d)[2d]$. The section compositions use the same module inverse-image compositors [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear].

source.place: Local construction, Rees etale chart and x_j=t u_j standard model

proof.text: Let $\tau_i:a_i^*A_{S_i}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}(d)[2d]$ be Tate pullback [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The formula $\lambda_i=(a_i^*c_i)^{-1}\tau_i^{-1}f_i$ is an isomorphism from $F|_{\mathbf A^1_{S_i}}$ to $a_i^*(C|_{S_i})$. All three arrows have been specified: two use the counit-normalized locality and affine adjunction comparisons of Steps 4–6, and the middle arrow is canonical Tate pullback. No equality between this initial map at $1$ and $\theta_i$ is being assumed.

source.place: Local construction, composing the two chart identifications

proof.text: Use the inverse-image compositors [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] and $a_i i_1=1_{S_i}$ to regard $i_1^*\lambda_i$ as an isomorphism $i_1^*F\to C|_{S_i}$. Thus $h_i=(i_1^*\lambda_i)\theta_i^{-1}$ is an automorphism of $C|_{S_i}$, and $\lambda_i^{\mathrm{norm}}=a_i^*(h_i^{-1})\lambda_i$ is an isomorphism. Its restriction is $h_i^{-1}(i_1^*\lambda_i)=h_i^{-1}h_i\theta_i=\theta_i$. This proves exactly the normalization claimed, using the actual $\theta_i$ from Step 2. For $d=0$ the polynomial calculation has no $u_j$, the twist and shift are trivial, and the same computation applies. For the empty base all constructions and equations restrict to the empty sites.

proof_origin.place: Opening paragraph and Local construction; detailed counit comparisons and normalization
